title: Leave question words where the answer goes
summary: Ask with shénme, nǎlǐ, and shéi in the statement position instead of moving them to the front.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: Chinese does not send a question word to the front of the sentence. The question word simply sits in the slot the answer would fill: 你买什么? nǐ mǎi shénme? (what are you buying?) answers with 我买书 wǒ mǎi shū, and 她去哪里? tā qù nǎlǐ? (where is she going?) answers with 她去车站 tā qù chēzhàn. Rehearse that substitution in your head before you speak, and remember that asking twice in one sentence is fine and common: 谁什么时候到? shéi shénme shíhou dào? Practise by taking any statement and replacing one piece with a question word, changing nothing else.
